sections.h2: How do I reach the Mitchell County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Go to Suite 4 at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, NC 28705, on weekdays. Documents are recorded between 8:00 and 4:30, and the office closes on holidays. The county page lists extension 1402 on the main line, 828.688.2139, and the office's own website gives extension 1401 for questions about fees and recording.

Marriage licenses are issued from 8:00 to 4:00 and cost $60, payable by check, cash or money order. The office accepts cash, credit and debit cards, checks and money orders for recording. A fax line is 828-688-3666.

The office describes itself as a recording office only. State law bars the register and the staff from practicing law, so questions about what a deed should say go to an attorney.

sections.h2: What can I search in Mitchell County's online records?
sections.html:
The search site at mitchelldeeds.com holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. Older material, from 1861 through 1993, sits in an Index Book Viewer under the search menu.

That 1994 line matters for sellers of long-held mountain land. A deed of trust from the early nineties, a right-of-way, or a division of a family tract may appear only in the older books. The county's services list also covers vital records, an online vital request, document recording standards, index standards and a redaction of personal information page.

  • Search the current index under the seller's name and the prior owner's name.
  • Check the Index Book Viewer when the chain of title reaches back before 1994.
  • Write down every deed of trust you find and confirm each has a recorded satisfaction.

A closing attorney still performs the formal title search. Your own pass simply tells you whether surprises are likely.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Mitchell County?
sections.html:
The office's posted fee schedule cites G.S. 161-10 and lists the amounts below, which took effect October 1, 2016.

Mitchell County Register of Deeds posted fees
ItemPosted amount
Deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, $4.00 each page after
Other instruments, such as a deed$26.00 for 15 pages, $4.00 each page after
Plat$21.00 a page, 18 by 24 inch sheets only
UCC filing$38.00 for 1 to 2 pages, $45.00 for 3 to 10
SatisfactionNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional

A UCC filing over ten pages is $45.00 plus $2.00 for every page past ten. If a figure matters for your closing, call 828-688-2139 extension 1401 before you send a check.

sections.h2: Can I record a Mitchell County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The office offers e-recording through two vendors: Simplifile and CSC. Both are named on the office's e-recording page.

Title companies and attorneys typically use such services, which spares a trip to Bakersville and lets a closing happen without anyone driving a paper original up the mountain. Ask your closing attorney whether the firm submits electronically. If you are recording something yourself, such as a corrective deed or a gift deed, take it to Suite 4 during business hours.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Mitchell County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays, and the payment goes to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. G.S. 105-228.30 charges $1.00 for each $500 of price, or part of $500.

The county holds half and sends the state half, minus refunds and a 2 percent county allowance on the state portion. A parcel lying in two counties pays in the county that has the greater value.

The Census Bureau lists a middle owner-occupied value of $220,100 for 2020 to 2024 and 76.3 percent owner occupancy, so most Mitchell County homes are lived in by their owners. Your deed price, not any survey average, sets your actual tax.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter in Mitchell County?
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 says unrecorded transfers and options give way to lien creditors and paying purchasers, and that rank follows the time of registration. Registration happens at the county where the land sits, so Mitchell parcels are registered in Bakersville.

For a seller, the practical lesson is to learn when your buyer's deed is expected to hit the index. The register is chosen by county voters every two years under G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: How do I guard a Mitchell County property against deed fraud?
sections.html:
Sign up for the office's free Fraud Alert system, which alerts you if someone tries to change records tied to your property. It helps most with vacant, rental and inherited houses, and with seasonal homes whose owners live elsewhere.

  • Keep copies of every deed, release and satisfaction you receive.
  • Look up your name in the index once or twice a year.
  • Record inherited or gifted property promptly.

On a contract for deed, Chapter 47H covers one-to-four family homes priced at $5,000 or more with five or more payments. The seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days.

sections.h2: How does the Register of Deeds connect to the Mitchell County tax offices?
sections.html:
They sit apart but work on the same sale. The register records the deed, the Tax Collector at 61 Crimson Laurel Circle takes payment of the year's bill, and the Tax Assessor at Suite 5, next door to the register, handles relief applications. The collector warns that bills mail in August to the owner of record on January 1, so the closing papers should say who covers the year.

If you inherited a Mitchell County house, a cash buyer can close as-is and have a closing attorney record the deed, so title moves to the buyer at settlement.

faqs.q: What number do I call for Mitchell County recording questions?
faqs.a: Call 828-688-2139 and use extension 1401 for fees and recording, or extension 1402 for the register's line. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 4, Bakersville.

faqs.q: How far back do the online Mitchell County deed records go?
faqs.a: The online index holds real estate indexes and images from 1994 to the present. The 1861 through 1993 material is in the Index Book Viewer on the search menu.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to record a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. The posted fee schedule lists satisfaction as no fee.

faqs.q: Does the Mitchell County office accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile and CSC, the two vendors the office names on its e-recording page.

faqs.q: Can the Register of Deeds staff give legal advice about my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says it acts as a recording office only, and state law keeps the register and staff from practicing law. Ask an attorney about wording, title or rights.
